key_insight: The paper uses quantum teleportation as a real-time communication mechanism between musical agents, turning quantum states into expressive, improvisational interactions rather than exact replicas.
engineering_relevance: It suggests a NISQ-friendly multi-agent architecture for interactive music systems where controlled imperfections, fidelity, and state transfer can be tuned as part of the artistic design.
method: Encode melodic and rhythmic behavior as quantum states using SQPAM.
Structure agent state dynamics with Quantum Phase Estimation.
Link up to three agents in one quantum circuit with directed communication via quantum teleportation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports evaluation using melodic correlation, pitch-set distance, and state fidelity, showing a continuum between imitation and divergence under a tunable reinterpretation method.
watch_item: Performance may depend strongly on NISQ noise, decoherence, and circuit complexity, which could limit reliable scaling beyond a small number of agents.
paper_title: Teleportation Game: Quantum Teleportation in Multi-Agent Systems for Interactive Music
